scope: Targeted independent read-only review of corrected AKASHA contact idempotency control flow, not a claim of full production or browser validation.
resolved_findings: A stale or reloaded tab prioritizes its retained session UUID after another tab confirms and removes the common reference.
Unconfirmed feedback locks all four payload fields; an ordinary retry keeps the same exact snapshot content.
An admission rejection preserves uncertainty when a previous UUID was observed instead of treating the earlier attempt as definitely absent.
The tab observes and persists an existing UUID before requesting the Web Lock, preserving uncertainty on immediate lock refusal.
The code also rechecks shared state under the lock so a UUID that appeared during acquisition is recognized as recovery.
Acknowledgement is set before cleanup; storage cleanup exceptions cannot overturn a matching success receipt.
Cleanup compares UUIDs and cannot delete another newer common operation id.
Unmount or late response does not clear the retained UUID or display a stale success.
Server replay validates exact id and payload and does not issue new provider emails.
validation_method: Static control-flow and diff review. Parent executes real Chromium Web Locks/hash scenarios and full test/type/build gates; another agent executes native PostgreSQL route validation. Those results are not claimed here.
scope_limits: Recovery after reload matches the exact payload fingerprint; draft text itself is intentionally not persisted.
No claim of live provider delivery or production deployment.
supersedes_findings: evidence/recovery-existing/review-and-recovery-result.json code_review findings, for the input hashes listed above only
